title: Constitutional Protection of Environment — Articles 21, 48A and 51A(g)

content.overview: The Constitution of India protects the environment through the right to life under Article 21 (read to include a healthy environment in judicial doctrine), the Directive Principle in Article 48A directing the State to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife, and the fundamental duty in Article 51A(g) requiring every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment. Remedies may be sought under Article 32 or Article 226 where maintainable. Article 48A is not enforceable as a fundamental right; Article 51A(g) is a citizen duty.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Art. 21 healthy-environment plea? (2) Art. 48A State duty? (3) Art. 51A(g) citizen duty? (4) Art. 32/226 maintainability vs NGT statutory route?
content.study:
Constitutional protection is layered: justiciable rights (Art. 21 doctrine), non-enforceable Directive Principles (Art. 48A), and duties (Art. 51A(g)). Statutory fora (NGT, pollution boards) often provide the primary remedial path.

Cases already in related environment files (retained for context when issue matches): Vellore; M.C. Mehta line. No new case invented.

sections.heading: Article 21
sections.body: Right to life has been judicially interpreted to include the right to a healthy environment; specific holdings remain on the case-law verification gate.

sections.heading: Article 48A
sections.body: Directive Principle — State shall endeavour to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard the forests and wild life of the country. Not enforceable by itself under Art. 37.

sections.heading: Article 51A(g)
sections.body: Fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.

sections.heading: Remedial routes
sections.body: Art. 32 (Supreme Court) and Art. 226 (High Court) where maintainable; NGT for Schedule I statutory environmental civil questions.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify whether the claim is constitutional, statutory, or both; do not treat Art. 48A as a freestanding writ right.

examples.title: Constitutional environmental PIL
examples.body: Petitioner invokes Art. 21 read with Art. 48A/51A(g) for environmental protection; court may also direct statutory compliance under EPA/Water/Air frameworks.

hypotheticals.question: Can a petitioner enforce Article 48A alone as a fundamental right?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Article 48A is a Directive Principle and is not enforceable by any court under Article 37, though it informs State duty and may guide interpretation.

distinctions.title: Article 48A vs Article 21
distinctions.left: Directive Principle — State endeavour; not court-enforceable as such.
distinctions.right: Fundamental right — justiciable; healthy-environment reading is doctrinal.

misconceptions.trap: Article 48A is a fundamental right enforceable like Article 21.
misconceptions.correction: Article 48A is a Directive Principle; it is fundamental in governance but not enforceable by courts as a right.
